title: No dispute that certainty of justification suffices for peace and thanksgiving
source_text: XXXII. Praeterea hic non controversitur, An certitudo & fiducia illa quam fideles possunt & debent habere de justificatione & adoptione sua, tanta sit ut sufficiat ad pellendam omnem mentis anxietatem, & tranquillitatem ac pacem conscientiae gignendam, fidelesque monendos ad hoc ut serio & toto affectu, de tanto beneficio Dei gratias agant. Utrinque enim res est in confesso, nec negatur a Doctoribus Ecclesiae Romanae.
pass_a_gloss: Besides, here it is not controverted whether that certainty and trust which the faithful can and ought to have concerning their justification and adoption is so great that it suffices for driving away every anxiety of mind, and for generating tranquillity and peace of conscience, and for admonishing the faithful to this, that seriously and with whole affection they give thanks to God for so great a benefit. For on both sides the matter is confessed, nor is it denied by the doctors of the Roman Church.
pass_b_english: Both sides grant that justified believers’ certainty can quiet anxiety and underwrite thanksgiving.
Roman doctors do not deny that such trust belongs to peace of conscience.
